about: Every frame of the board as its own PNG at native size (1280 x 720), with its caption. board.png is the sheet of 1:1 crops of these.

frames.title: A  ·  Ink outline, dotted fall line, dashed spread  ·  planning zoom
frames.caption: Ink outline, dotted fall line, dashed spread: the planning zoom 0.35, the aim at the ideal release angle. All linework and nothing filled, so the village reads straight through. The cone is an inked rim; a dotted line runs from where the bomber lets go (the dot on its path) to the aim; the spread is a dashed ellipse. Accuracy is said by the ellipse's size and the lettering alone.

frames.title: B  ·  Wash in the side colour, crosshair, faint spread  ·  planning zoom
frames.caption: Wash in the side colour, crosshair, faint spread: the planning zoom 0.35, the aim at the ideal release angle. The cone as a wash in the unit's side colour, deepest round the ideal aim and fading to the rim: the more colour under the aim, the closer the release is to ideal. The same wash Alex chose for the guns' cones (decision cone-overlay), used for bombs. A crosshair at the aim, a faint inked ellipse for the spread.

frames.title: C  ·  Stippled cone, spread as scattered impacts  ·  planning zoom
frames.caption: Stippled cone, spread as scattered impacts: the planning zoom 0.35, the aim at the ideal release angle. The cone in dots, dense toward the ideal aim and thin to the rim; the spread is not an outline but a scatter of dots, the places bombs may land (the same dots every frame, so nothing shimmers). Reads as the bombs' own randomness.

frames.title: D  ·  Range rings from the release point  ·  planning zoom
frames.caption: Range rings from the release point: the planning zoom 0.35, the aim at the ideal release angle. A faint wash and RANGE RINGS about the release point, one every 100 m through the cone, the aim's own ring solid: the throw is the thing, and this draws it as a distance. The spread is a solid ellipse. The most technical of the four.
